::: {.exercise-include target-level="2"}
# Loop output {#sec-loop-output}

What does the loop print?

```vb
For i = 1 To 3
    Debug.Print i * 2
Next i
```

::: {.alpha-list}
A) 1, 2, 3
B) [2, 4, 6]{.correct}
C) 2, 4, 6, 8
D) 3, 6, 9
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Solution"}
::: {.alpha-explanations}
A) Prints `i` instead of `i * 2`.
B) [Doubles each of the three values of `i`.]{.correct}
C) Runs the loop one extra time.
D) Multiplies by three.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.exercise-include target-level="2"}
# Summing a list {#sec-summing}

Which listing returns the sum of the values in `v`?

::: {.alpha-list}
A) @lst-sum-a
B) [@lst-sum-b]{.correct}
C) @lst-sum-c
D) @lst-sum-d
:::

:::: {#lst-sum layout-ncol="2"}
::: {#lst-sum-a}
```vb
total = 0
For i = 1 To n - 1
    total = total + v(i)
Next i
```
Stops one short.
:::

::: {#lst-sum-b}
```vb
total = 0
For i = 1 To n
    total = total + v(i)
Next i
```
Adds every value.
:::

::: {#lst-sum-c}
```vb
For i = 1 To n
    total = 0
    total = total + v(i)
Next i
```
Resets inside the loop.
:::

::: {#lst-sum-d}
```vb
total = 1
For i = 1 To n
    total = total * v(i)
Next i
```
Multiplies.
:::

Four ways to sum `v(1)` to `v(n)` (Question [-@sec-summing]).
::::

::: {.callout-note title="Solution"}
::: {.alpha-explanations}
A) @lst-sum-a misses the last value.
B) [@lst-sum-b adds every value once.]{.correct}
C) @lst-sum-c keeps only the last value.
D) @lst-sum-d computes a product.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.exercise-include target-level="2"}
# Two correct listings {#sec-pairs}

Which pair of listings both return the larger of `x` and `y`?

::: {.alpha-list}
A) [@lst-max-a and @lst-max-b]{.correct}
B) @lst-max-b and @lst-max-c
C) @lst-max-c and @lst-max-d
D) @lst-max-a and @lst-max-d
:::

:::: {#lst-max layout-ncol="2"}
::: {#lst-max-a}
```vb
If x > y Then m = x Else m = y
```
With If.
:::

::: {#lst-max-b}
```vb
m = WorksheetFunction.Max(x, y)
```
With Max.
:::

::: {#lst-max-c}
```vb
If x < y Then m = x Else m = y
```
Reversed test.
:::

::: {#lst-max-d}
```vb
m = x
```
Ignores `y`.
:::

Four ways to find the larger value (Question [-@sec-pairs]).
::::

::: {.callout-note title="Solution"}
::: {.alpha-explanations}
A) [Both pick the larger value.]{.correct}
B) @lst-max-c returns the smaller value.
C) Neither listing is correct.
D) @lst-max-d ignores `y`.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.exercise-include target-level="2"}
# A solution as a list {#sec-declare}

Which statement declares an integer?

::: {.alpha-list}
A) `Dim n As String`
B) `Dim n As Double`
C) [`Dim n As Integer`]{.correct}
D) `Dim n As Boolean`
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Solution"}
::: {.alpha-explanations}
A) Declares text.
B) Declares a decimal number.
C) [Declares a whole number.]{.correct}
D) Declares `True` or `False`.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.exercise-include target-level="2"}
# An option that refers to the others {#sec-none}

Which value does `CInt("3.7")` return?

::: {.alpha-list}
A) 3
B) [4]{.correct}
C) 3.7
D) None of the above
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Solution"}
`CInt` rounds to the nearest integer, so it returns 4.
:::
:::
